method: Windows Computer Use; real packaged Tauri WebView2, OS window creation/close, OS save picker, then separate raw CFB and engine readback
observations: Relative frontend path loads the embedded app at http://tauri.localhost/; old absolute path incorrectly showed a file:// directory listing.
Alt+N created a second native window with a UUID-owned context; main remained a separate one-tab blank workspace.
Clicked document canvas and entered CHILD WINDOW RECOVERY 68; visible text and dirty state verified.
Ctrl+Alt+T created a second tab within that same child window and preserved the first dirty tab.
Alt+F4 displayed the four-choice exit dialog. Keep recovery exited that child; a fresh window listing proved its absence and main presence.
Main File menu registry showed the same scope as recovery kept. Reopening created a new native window with that exact scope and both tabs.
Selecting the first restored tab showed the exact text and dirty state.
The actual OS save picker saved child-recovered.hwp to an isolated build path. Native UI reported saved and cleared dirty.
Separate raw CFB PARA_TEXT read found the marker once; engine exact text, both-format strict reopen, live and disk immutability passed.

failedBuildRetained.issue: Absolute Windows frontendDist parsed as URL, producing a directory listing. That executable was not a working app validation.

limits: This immutable GUI build contains engine68, not later engine candidates or the new Agent file commands.
No claim of all Hancom import/export formats, XML schemas, full metadata history, forced power failure or whole product parity.
The unchanged previous user app and Hancom documents were left open; no API credentials or private workspace data are packaged.
The build manifest retains launched=false from preparation. This separate actual report records subsequent GUI actions.
